newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds fell in the afternoon after news U.S. December nonfarm payrolls were higher than expected, but prices were able to recover late in the day.
U.S. December payrolls rose by 262,000 jobs, above the 192,00 gain forecast.

The U.S. T-bond futures contract was down nearly 1-1/2 points after the news. The Swiss Confederate bond March futures contract also fell from levels just below the December 20 contract high of 116.37. But it recovered late in the day. The 4-1/2 percent June 2007 cash bond also ended higher, yielding 3.909 percent versus 3.929 percent on Thursday.
"The market did come off after the figures. It probably lost about 15 ticks. But I personally hardly saw any volume," one Swiss-based trader said.
"I would say the market is very resilient. I think we could go a tick weaker, still. But I would definitely be a buyer on dips," the trader added.

Telenor, the Norwegian telecom firm, launched a 150 million Swiss franc bond due August 2001, with a 2-3/4 percent coupon priced at 101.15. The issue was quoted by lead UBS yielding 2.86 percent UIXK. Traders said demand was relatively good for the issue, but domestic borrowers continued to be favoured.
Traders said foreign corporate borrowers were in abundance, while Swiss domestic borrowers remained relatively scarce.
New foreign issues, including reopenings, totaled nearly 2.0 billion francs so far this year. Swiss domestic offerings, by contrast, have totaled only 300 million.
Mar Conf futures CONFH7 up two at 116.12.
Mar Comi medium-term bond COMIH7 up five at 111.10
Mar Euro Swiss francs FESH7 down two at 98.14.
